Date November 14, 1936
Subject Examination of documents reported to have issued by
General Yi T'ang
Made by ____ and ____ Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

An examination of the attached two documents
reported to have been "Warrants of Appointment"
issued by General YI T'ANG, Commander of the New
4th Route Army show that the characters therein
were very poorly written, most probably by a person
(both by the same person) without much experience
in Chinese writing. The chop of the Commander of
the New 4th Route Army on the documents and on the
envelope are unusually small and poorly engraved.
Contrary to usual custom, the chop of the Commander
appears in the centre instead of on the last page
of the "Warrant of Appointment." Besides there
should have been a printed heading in the document
such as "Commander of the 4th Route Army" or
"Office of the 4th Route Army" which precede the
wording (in writing) "So and so is hereby appointed"
and this was omitted in the two documents and the
paper produced is commonly used in writing petitions
and can be easily secured from any stationery shops.
Further it is quite unusual particularly at this
moment and especially in the Settlement, for a
person receiving an appointment from Chungking
Government to carry a document for his identity
or to let others have the document as evidence
against him.

1st Accused

Tsoo Yu Zung(朱友綜).
Soochow X D. S. I. Pryde
O.R.R.Q. 9-11-30 Clock Hse

My name is Tsoo Yu Sung(朱友笙) alias Tsoo Chah Sung
age 28, native of Soochow and I live at Lane 73, House 6
Nylungh Rd. I was born in Soochow. My father was the com-
pradore of Vol. Ltd & Co., Shanghai. He died when I was
about eight years old. Soon after I was born my mother died
and I was brought to Shanghai as an infant. From the age of
eight years to 13 years I was educated at a Chinese Primary
School in Nartao. From 13 to 14 years at the S.M.C. Polytech-
nic School, Pahkai Rd. From 14 years to 23 years at the
Kwang Hua College, Great Western Rd. On leaving college I
became employed as an Insurance Broker with the Ling Shao Fire
& Marine Insurance Co, State Bank Bldg, Peking Rd, and re-
mained with them until the commencement of hostilities in 1937.
Since 1938 I have been employed with the China Insurance Co.,
Ltd., 590 Szechuen Road.

I am also a partner together with my younger brother
named Tsoo Yu Chang(朱友璋) in the Yu Shing Realty Co., which
is an inheritance from my father. We own the house in the
Yue Shing Li, Ginkling Rd. Only the houses belong to us, the
land actually belongs to Miss Hartwell. We also own property
situated at Lanes 63 and 70 Nylungh Rd. Both the land and
houses here belong to us entirely. The property is registered
with Lester, Morris & Co.

I have lived in Shanghai all my life and I have never
had any connections with the Communist or other party nor I ever
had any political leanings. I do not know of any reason why
I should be arrested. Last year I had trouble with my tenants
pages.zh:
第一被告

朱友综（Tsoo Yu Zung）。
苏州 X 侦探副督察长 Pryde
O.R.R.Q. 1930年11月9日 时钟屋

我叫朱友笙（Tsoo Yu Sung），又名朱查笙（Tsoo Chah Sung），
28岁，苏州人，现住尼伦路（Nyburgh Rd.）73弄6号。我出生于苏州。我的父亲是上海Vol. Ltd & Co.公司的买办。他在我大约八岁时去世。我不久出生后母亲也去世了，我还是婴儿时就被带到上海。从八岁到十三岁，我在南市的一所华立小学读书。从十三岁到十四岁，我在白克路（Pahkai Rd.）的工部局 polytechnic 学校读书。从十四岁到二十三岁，我在大西路的光华大学读书。大学毕业后，我在北京路国家银行大楼的灵绍水火保险公司受雇为保险经纪人，并一直在那里工作直到1937年战事爆发。自1938年以来，我一直在四川北路590号的中国保险公司有限公司工作。

我也是余兴房地产公司的合伙人，合伙人是我的弟弟朱友璋（Tsoo Yu Chang），该公司是我父亲的遗产。我们拥有金陵路悦兴里的房屋。只有房子属于我们，土地实际上属于哈特韦尔小姐（Miss Hartwell）。我们还拥有位于尼伦路63弄和70弄的房产。这里的土地和房屋完全属于我们。该房产在莱斯特·莫里斯公司（Lester, Morris & Co.）注册。

我一生都住在上海，从未与共产党或其他政党有任何联系，也从未有过任何政治倾向。我不知道我为什么会被逮捕。去年我与租户发生过纠纷

pages.en:
(2)

in the Yue Shing Li over the increase of the water rate and
a letter was received by the S.M.Police at that time implicat-
ing one in the murder of Mr. Leh Lien Kwei. Mr. Crighton
of S.M.Police Headquarters made enquiries regarding same and
we suspected at the time that these dissatisfied tenants
may have been the writer of this letter. Mr. Crighton knows
the full facts regarding this.

I also wish to state that on September 14, 1939
three Japanese in plain cloths came to my house at about
7 a.m. These Japanese who spoke broken Chinese asked for the
master of the house. I came out and they questioned me
regarding my name etc., which they did not appear to believe.
At about 8 a.m. they took me to Hongkew in a motor car. They
forced me to leave my house, although I did not actually
resist. I was taken to a building at the rear of the New Asia
Hotel. This building was formerly the Wing On Banking Corp.
I was taken to a room on the 3rd. floor where I was questioned
by a Japanese in plain clothes, through a Chinese interpreter,
regarding the smuggling of sand. They mentioned a number of
names, but I did not know any of them. By 11.30 a.m. they
apparently became convinced that I was not concerned in the
smuggling of sand, and I was released. As I had no pass for
Hongkew the Chinese interpreter escorted me to the Bridge. I
then returned to my home on Myburgh Road and same day went to
live with my uncle on Ave Edward, French Concession for two
weeks, after which I returned to my house. I did not report
this case to the police.
pages.zh:
(2)

在悦兴里因水费上涨问题，当时上海公共租界警务处收到一封信，牵连到黎连贵先生（Mr. Leh Lien Kwei）被谋杀案中的一人。上海公共租界警务处总部的克莱顿先生（Mr. Crighton）对此进行了调查，我们当时怀疑这些不满的租户可能是这封信的作者。克莱顿先生了解此事的全部事实。

我还想说明，1939年9月14日上午7点左右，三名便衣日本人来到我家。这些讲着蹩脚中文的日本人要求见户主。我出来以后，他们询问了我的姓名等情况，但他们似乎并不相信。上午8点左右，他们用汽车把我带到虹口。他们强迫我离开家，虽然我并没有真正反抗。我被带到新亚酒店后面的一栋大楼。这栋大楼以前是永安银行公司。我被带到三楼的一个房间，一名便衣日本人通过一名中文翻译对我进行讯问，内容是关于走私沙子的事。他们提到了一些名字，但我一个都不认识。到了上午11点30分，他们显然确信我与走私沙子无关，于是将我释放。由于我没有虹口的通行证，那名中文翻译护送我到了桥头。然后我回到了迈尔西爱路（Myburgh Road）的家，当天就去法租界爱德华大道（Ave Edward）的叔叔家住了两周，之后才回到自己家。我没有向警方报告此案。

pages.en:
(3)

Regarding my younger brother, he is actually a
half-brother, being born of the same father but a different
mother. My relationship with him is not harmonious. We live
together in the same house, but the house is so divided that
we do not meet very often, as he lives on the West side with
his mother (my step-mother), and I live with my wife and
family on the East side. Although he is my partner in the Yu
Shing Realty Co., he takes no active part in this business.
I know that he has a girl friend named Zee Yung Yah
(徐文俠), who previously lived on Tung Mung Road, Nantao.
I do not know where she lives now. She is of the very modern
type and so is my brother and I do not get along harmoniously
with them.
I last saw my brother on the evening of 7.11.39 when
we had a crab dinner together in our home.
Regarding the other two men who are arrested namely:
Yee On Sang (倪和生) and Tsou Wei Tao (朱渭), both
are my cousins. The former is employed by me as rent collector
and the latter as a clerk.

Signed:
pages.zh:
(3)

关于我的弟弟，他实际上是同父异母的兄弟，因为我们是同一个父亲但不同的母亲所生。我和他的关系不和睦。我们住在同一所房子里，但房子隔开了，所以我们不常见面，因为他和他的母亲（我的继母）住在西边，而我和我的妻子家人住在东边。虽然他是余兴房地产公司的合伙人，但他并不积极参与这项业务。我知道他有一个女朋友叫徐文俠（Zee Yung Yah），以前住在南市东门路。我不知道她现在住在哪里。她是非常现代的类型，我弟弟也是，我和他们相处得不融洽。
我最后一次见到我弟弟是在1939年11月7日晚上，当时我们在家里一起吃螃蟹晚餐。
关于另外两名被捕男子，即：
倪和生（Yee On Sang）和朱渭（Tsou Wei Tao），
他们都是我的表亲。前者受雇于我担任收租员，后者担任职员。

签名：

Yee Oo Sung(倪和生)
Soochow                                     x   D.S.I.Pryde
Co.B.M.C.             9-11-39                       Clerk Hsu

My name Yee Oo Sung(倪和生); age 34, native of
Soochow. I was born in Soochow and from the age of 7 years
to 13 years attended school in my native place. At the age
of 13 I came to Shanghai and studied at St. Peters School,
Avenue Rd. I then became apprenticed to the Tung Yih Native
Bank, Tientsin Rd. I remained with this bank until I was 20
years old, when it closed down. I then obtained a position
with the Wei Foong Bank, Tientsin Rd. and remained there until
the commencement of hostilities in 1937 when this bank also
closed down. I then returned to Soochow where my wife and
mother live and remained there until Jan. 1938. I was living
in the outskirts of Soochow at the time this town was taken
by the Japanese Forces but took no action on either side.
    On my return to Shanghai in Jan. 1938 I obtained a
position as a rent collector with the Yu Shing Realty Co.,
which is owned by my cousin (1st accused). I lived with my
cousin at 73/8 Nyburgh Road and have remained there ever since
My wife still lives in Soochow.

                                        Signed:
pages.zh:
倪和生（Yee Oo Sung）

我叫倪和生（Yee Oo Sung）；34岁，苏州人。我出生于苏州，从7岁到13岁在家乡上学。13岁时我来到上海，在爱文义路（Avenue Rd.）的圣彼得学校读书。随后我在天津路的通益钱庄当学徒。我一直在这家钱庄工作到20岁，那时钱庄倒闭了。随后我在天津路的伟丰银行找到了一份工作，并一直在那里工作到1937年战事爆发，该银行也倒闭了。然后我回到苏州，我的妻子和母亲住在那里，我一直待到1938年1月。日军占领苏州时，我住在苏州郊区，但没有参与任何一方的行动。
    1938年1月回到上海后，我在余兴房地产公司找到了一份收租员的工作，该公司由我的表兄（第一被告）所有。我和表兄一起住在尼伯路（Nyburgh Road）73/8号，并一直住在那里。我的妻子仍住在苏州。

Soochow                                            J. I. Pryde
C.F.H. . . (C.l)          9.11.49                   Clerk Hsu

My name is Tseu Wei Yue, age 31, native of Soochow.
I was born in Soochow and educated at a native school there
from the age of 8 years to 13 years. I then became an
apprentice in a pawnshop at Tanyang. At the age of 16 years
I came to Shanghai and obtained a position as shop assistant
in the Feong Wei Hoo (方惠和) Sugar Hong, Nantao. At the
age of 20 years I became shroff and salesman at the Shanghai
Dyeing Co. (上海精煉二廠), Pah Hwa Road, Chapei. I remained
in this position until the commencement of hostilities in
1937, when I returned to Soochow, where I stayed unemployed
until Feb. 1938. I then came to Shanghai and obtained a
position as clerk in the Yu Shing Realty Co., which is owned
by my cousin (1st accused). I lived together with my cousin
at 73/6 Nyburgh Road and have remained there ever since.
My wife, children and mother are at present in Soochow.

Signed.

我叫朱渭岳，31岁，苏州人。我出生于苏州，从8岁到13岁在当地的一所私塾读书。随后我在丹阳的一家当铺当学徒。16岁时我来到上海，在南市方惠和糖行找到了一份店员的工作。20岁时，我在闸北白华路的上海精炼二厂（Shanghai Dyeing Co.）成为出纳员和推销员。我一直在这个职位上工作到1937年战事爆发，当时我回到苏州，在那里失业直到1938年2月。随后我来到上海，在余兴房地产公司找到了一份职员的工作，该公司由我的表兄（第一被告）所有。我和表兄一起住在尼伯路（Nyburgh Road）73/6号，并一直住在那里。我的妻子、孩子和母亲目前在苏州。

Further to Diary No.1. At 4.45 a.m. on
9.11.39 Sub-Inspector Furuki and five other members
of the C.C.P. Bureau came to C.B.H.Q. and stated they
wished to visit House 6, Lane 73 Wyburgh Road to arrest
two men named:-
    Tseu Yu Jeng (朱友然) and
    Tseu Yu Ching (朱友清)
who were the Commander and Adjutant respectively of the
Supply Unit of the 4th. Route Army and active in the
Woosung - Shanghai Area. Sub-Inspector Furuki also
stated that some of the subordinates of these two men
may also be on the premises, and if so he would also
like to have these arrested.

    The U.S. Marine Headquarters and Siam Police
Station were informed of the vicinity of the impending
raid at 5 a.m. and assistance was rendered by D.S.I.s
Pryde and Yang Chi Kwang, D.S.os Bannington and Sugimoto,
D.P.S. Yamahara, C.D.S.s 184 and 211 and the stated
address visited at 5.15 a.m. The house proved to be
a large Chinese house and considerable difficulty was
experienced in gaining entrance, but after about half
hour the inmates were convinced and entrance effected.
All the rooms were visited in turn and all the inmates

继日记第1号之后。1939年11月9日凌晨4时45分，古木（Furuki）巡官及华中警察总局其他五名成员来到中央捕房总部（C.B.H.Q.），表示他们希望前往威伯克路（Wyburgh Road）73弄6号逮捕两名男子，姓名如下：
    朱友然 (Tseu Yu Jeng) 和
    朱友清 (Tseu Yu Ching)
二人分别为新四军供给部指挥官和副官，在吴淞-上海地区活动。古木巡官还指出，这两人的部分下属可能也在该处，如果是这样，他也希望将这些人员逮捕。

美国海军陆战队总部和暹罗捕房已获知即将在凌晨5时进行的突袭行动附近区域的情况，并由副巡官普赖德（Pryde）和杨志光（Yang Chi Kwang）、副巡长班宁顿（Bannington）和杉本（Sugimoto）、警佐山原（Yamahara）、中国籍侦探184号和211号提供了协助，并于凌晨5时15分抵达上述地址。该房屋被证明是一栋大型中式住宅，进入时遇到了相当大的困难，但经过约半小时后，屋内人员被说服，得以进入。所有房间依次搜查，所有屋内人员

pages.en:
2/2

assembled in the main room. Enquiries showed that the
house belongs to two brothers named Tsen Yu Zung and
Tsen Yu Ching, who are the persons whom the C.C.P.B.
wished to arrest. The former was present and placed
under arrest, but the latter was absent. Two other
men, both of whom are cousins of the 1st. named were
also arrested. The names and particulars of the arrested
follow:-

1st. accused Tsen Yu Zung (朱友然), 28, Soochow,
m/Insurance Agent and proprietor of the Yue
Shing (悦兴) Realty Co.

2nd. accused Yeo Oo Sang (倪和生), 34, Soochow,
m/Rent Collector of the Yue Shing Realty Co.

3rd. accused Tsen Wei Yao (朱渭漁), 31, Soochow,
m/Clerk of the Yue Shing Realty Co.

Only a superficial search of the house was made.
The remaining inmates of the house who are the step-
mother of the 1st. accused, the wives and relations of
the arrested men and male and female employees were not
arrested.

The police party left the house at 7.10 a.m.
Whilst the police were on the premises at 6.40 a.m. a
party from Siam Station arrived under D.S. Bradley,
all three having been turned in to Siam Station by a
pages.zh:
2/2

聚集在主屋。经查询，该房屋属于两兄弟，名为曾友宗（Tsen Yu Zung）和曾友清（Tsen Yu Ching），即华中警察总局希望逮捕的人员。前者在场并被逮捕，但后者不在场。另外两名男子也被逮捕，两人均为第一被告的堂兄弟。被捕者姓名及详情如下：

第一被告 曾友宗（朱友然）(Tsen Yu Zung)，28岁，苏州人，已婚/保险代理人及悦兴房地产公司业主。

第二被告 倪和生 (Yeo Oo Sang)，34岁，苏州人，已婚/悦兴房地产公司收租员。

第三被告 朱渭漁 (Tsen Wei Yao)，31岁，苏州人，已婚/悦兴房地产公司职员。

仅对房屋进行了表面搜查。屋内其余人员，包括第一被告的继母、被捕者的妻子和亲属以及男女雇员，均未逮捕。

警方于上午7时10分离开该房屋。当警方在上午6时40分仍在现场时，由副巡长布拉德利（Bradley）率领的一队人马从暹罗捕房抵达，这三人都被一名邻居扭送至暹罗捕房。由于布拉德利副巡长意识到中央捕房总部的一队人马就在附近，因此未发生任何意外事件。

pages.en:
2/3

neighbour. As D.S. Bradley realized a party from
C.B.H.Q. was in this vicinity, no untoward incident
occurred.

On return to C.B.H.Q., Sub-Inspector Furuki
produced two documents which he states were handed
to him by his informer and which are the appointments
of Tsau Yu Jung (1st. accused) and Tsau Yu Ching (not
arrested) as officers of the 4th. Route Army. These
documents are in process of translation. Sub-Inspector
Furuki requests that these three men be detained pending
further enquiries being made from his informer. Statement
are being taken from the arrested men.

Subject Translation of documents seized at Lane 258, 99 Wuting Road
on April 24th, 1940. (C.1 Misc.55/40).

Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

Attached hereto are summarized translations
of documents seized by C.1 (Crime Branch) at Lane 258,
99 Wuting Road, where two male Chinese named Dau Foong
( 陶 峰 ) and Shah Liang ( 夏 良 ) were arrested at
the request of the Japanese Gendarmerie.

Particulars of the person Dau Foong appear
in Special Branch records and are given hereunder.
He is mentioned together with several others connected
with mobile units operating in the Shanghai hinterland.
(1) Dau Foong Chief of a mobile unit operating in
Chuensha, Nanwei, Pootung (Hwa Mei
Pao, 6-9-38). One of the commanders
of the Loyal & Righteous National
Salvation Army under the Command of the
Kiangsu Provincial Government operating
in the Pootung Peninsula and areas
abutting the Shanghai-Hangchow Railway.
(Special Branch report, S.889, 14-11-39).
(2) Hsu Hung Fah or Zee Hung Fah ( 徐 洪 發 )
Ex-guerilla commander in Pootung.
Appointed by Japanese as Commander of
the so-called Chuensha Self Defence
Corps in Pootung during April, 1939,
with Headquarters at Tso Kia Jao,
Pootung. (Special Branch report S.889,
14-11-39).

由 D. I. Crawford 制作并转发。

随函附上刑事处（C.1）在武定路99号258弄缴获文件的摘要译文，在该处应日本宪兵队的请求逮捕了两名中国男子，名为陶峰（Dau Foong）和夏良（Shah Liang）。

陶峰的个人详情见于特别处档案，现列于下方。他与数名其他在上海 hinterland（腹地）活动的流动部队人员一同被提及。
(1) 陶峰，在川沙、南汇、浦东活动的流动部队首领（华美报，1938年9月6日）。江苏省政府指挥下的忠义救国军指挥官之一，该军在浦东半岛及毗邻沪杭铁路的地区活动。（特别处报告，S.889，1939年11月14日）。

List of documents seized on April 24, 1940, at
Lane 258, 99 Wuting Road (office of the Shanghai
Municipality Distressed Children's Nursery) where
Dau Foong (戴 豐) alias Dau Ching Yan (戴 清 然)
and Shah Liang (夏 良) were arrested.

1. Petition, dated April 23, 1940, addressed to General
Koo Tso Tung, Commander-in-chief of 3rd War Zone
(Chekiang, etc.), from Dau Foong (in custody), "Major-
General in Command of the 7th Route of Guerillas in
Southern Kiangsu; communication address: Pootung
Guild, 1454 Avenue Edward VII."
Summary of contents:
Since the withdrawal of Chinese troops from Shanghai,
the petitioner has been conducting guerilla warfare at
Shanghai. He has submitted several petitions but
received no reply. He now requests that officers be
appointed to inspect and reorganise his men.

2. A similar petition addressed to General Ho Ying Ching,
Minister of War. (same date)

3. A similar petition addressed to General Chiang Kai Shek.
(same date)

4 - 8. Five books containing a record of letters received and
dispatched by Dau Foong between November, 1939, and
March, 1940.

9. One book marked "Shun Dzoe" (興 社) containing names
only of 25 persons including Zing Shing Yen (秦 興 炎).
(ex-guerilla commander in Pootung having surrendered to
Japanese)

10. One book marked "Recollections", containing an account
of the rebellion by Dau Foong's subordinates, Zing Shing
Yen (秦 興 炎), Zau Vee Tseu (曹 維 鳳), Tsang Chuen
Pah (張 川 百), Koo King San (顧 金 山), Hsu Ts Fee
(許 志 飛) who surrendered to the Japanese during
July, 1939, and a report on Zee Hung Fah's (徐 洪 發),
another subordinate of Dau, joining the Japanese.

11. Book containing names of officers and men of the 2nd
Main Group of Zee Hung Fah's People's Self Defence Group.

12. Account book (petty cash accounts).

13. Letter addressed by Dau Foong to Woo Zau Da (吳 紹 達),
Executive Committee of local Kuomintang, requesting the
latter to apply to "Central" on his behalf for appointment
and disposal of his men.

14. Lists of officers and men of Zee Hung Fah's People's
to 20. Self Defence Group.

21. List of names of 58 persons purporting to be members of
the local Kuomintang.

22. Draft of an order appointing one Yu En Ta (俞 恩 達)
to the post of Training Officer attached to the Political
Section of 1st Section of "this Headquarters".

1940年4月24日在吴廷路99号258弄（上海市难童 nursery 办公室）逮捕戴丰（Dau Foong，又名戴清然 Dau Ching Yan）和夏良（Shah Liang）时查获的文件清单。

1. 请愿书一份，日期为1940年4月23日，由戴丰（在押）致第三战区（浙江等地）司令长官顾祝同将军。戴丰自称“苏南游击第七路指挥官”；通讯地址：爱多亚路1454号浦东会馆。
内容摘要：
自中国军队撤离上海以来，申请人一直在上海进行游击战。他曾提交数份请愿书，但未获回复。现请求派员视察并整编其部属。

2. 类似请愿书一份，致军政部长何应钦将军。（同日）

3. 类似请愿书一份，致蒋介石将军。（同日）

4 - 8. 五本簿册，记载戴丰于1939年11月至1940年3月期间收发的信件。

9. 一本标记为“兴社”（Shun Dzoe）的簿册，仅载有包括秦兴炎（Zing Shing Yen）在内的25人姓名。（秦兴炎系前浦东游击队指挥官，已向日军投降）

10. 一本标记为“回忆录”的簿册，记载戴丰下属秦兴炎、曹维凤（Zau Vee Tseu）、张川百（Tsang Chuen Pah）、顾金山（Koo King San）、许志飞（Hsu Ts Fee）于1939年7月间向日军投降的叛变经过，以及戴的另一名下属徐洪发（Zee Hung Fah）投敌的报告。

11. 一本簿册，载有徐洪发人民自卫团第二总队的官兵名单。

12. 账簿一本（零用现金账）。

13. 戴丰致当地国民党执行委员会吴绍达（Woo Zau Da）的信函，请求后者代为向“中央”申请对其部属的委任及处置事宜。

14. 至 20. 徐洪发人民自卫团的官兵名单。

21. 声称是当地国民党成员的58人姓名清单。

22. 任命俞恩达（Yu En Ta）为“本总部”第一处政治科训练官的命令草稿。

23. Sheet of paper containing the following inscriptions

Lee Chien Ming {李健民}

25. Note, dated March 20, 1940, issued by Colonel Zia

26. One intelligence report issued to newspaper offices by

27. One copy of Anti-Wang Ching Wei handbill, urging students

28. Another handbill of a similar strain.

29. A note from Han Kuo (韓鳳) dated "12/2", requesting

Yang Mau Sung {楊茂松}
Daung Yui Wen {董玉文}
Dau Ho Tsung {杜和種}
Daung Foh Dau {董佛度}
Chen Tsung {陳宗}
Loh Loong Sung {羅龍生}
Lee Tsun Tung {李尊東}

30. One letter written on three sheets of note paper and
to 32. signed by Han Kuo (韓鳳) and Loh Voong Ziang

Contents
Reporting on the punishment of some members
on charges of disloyalty and the receipt of
threatening letters from Shanghai thereafter.

33. One letter on three sheets of note paper signed by Han
to 35. Kuo, arguing that there should no leniency in dealing
with disloyal members.

- 3 -

36. Draft of a note offering thanks for assistance in
national salvation work. (no names or other particulars)

37. Note addressed to "younger brother Tsung Tung" (征東)
from Dau Foong to the effect that the addressee should
tell the truth about the circumstances surrounding his
detention at "Ka" (? Kading) or he would be dealt with
without leniency.

38. Note containing the following :-
Jeng Han Sung (岑漢生),
aged 50, native of Hokien, has
worked for eight years in an
arsenal in Kwangtung, repairing
firearms.
Loh Wen Tsung (陸文宗),
aged 30, native of Soochow, is
a repairer.

39. Letter from Dau Oen (溫安) to Wen Ping (文賓),
undated, stating that Lee Tsung Tung (李征東)
has been detained on account of suspicious movements
and that Mr. Tan. (譚 ) has requested to deal with
him leniently and Mr. Ting Loo Die (丁魯弟) and
others have been requested to help him.

40. Letter dated February 13, 1940, addressed to Dau Oen
(溫安) from Lee Tsung Tung reporting on his detention
and requesting Dau to interview Mr. Tan (譚 ) in Tung
Fang Hotel in order to effect his release.

41 Draft of a petition addressed to General Chiang Kai
to 42. Shek requesting appointment, and draft of a letter.

43 Notes of a speech by Dau Foong on his appointment
to 44. as "Commander of the 7th Route".

45. Paper containing rough notes of Dau Foong's antecedents.

46 Draft of manifesto addressed to fellow countrymen by
to 48. Dau Foong on his work for the nation.

49. Draft of a letter addressed to Lee Ts Ming (李志明)
by Dau Foong reporting on the "rebellion" of his
subordinates.

50. Letter from Zee Ts Dau (徐志道) applying for
employment, September 26.

51. Mimeographed circular issued in the names of Dau Foong
and Nyi Ting Lai (倪聽雷) advising Zee Hung Fah
not to surrender to the enemy.

52 Five lists of "relatives and friends".
to 56.

57. Printed circular issued by Japanese Military at Chuenaha
instructing people to leave places under the control of
Zing Shing Yen (秦興炎) as an attack will be launched
on his men.

58. Letter dated July 26, 1938, from Ting Lien (聽 靈 ) to
Dau (溫 ) reporting on situation in Pootung.

36. 感谢协助救国工作的便条草稿。（无姓名或其他详情）

37. 戴丰致“征东弟”（Tsung Tung）的便条，大意是受件人应如实交代其在“嘉”（？嘉定）被拘留的情况，否则将从严处理。

38. 便条一份，内容如下：
岑汉生（Jeng Han Sung），
50岁，福建人，
曾在广东兵工厂工作八年，修理枪械。
陆文宗（Loh Wen Tsung），
30岁，苏州人，
修理工。

39. 温安（Dau Oen）致文宾（Wen Ping）的信函，未注日期，称李征东（Lee Tsung Tung）因行动可疑被拘留，谭先生（Mr. Tan.）请求对其从宽处理，并已请求丁鲁弟（Ting Loo Die）等人予以帮助。

40. 李征东致温安（Dau Oen）的信函，日期为1940年2月13日，报告其被拘留情况，并请求戴前往东方饭店会见谭先生（Mr. Tan），以促成其释放。

41. 至 42. 致蒋介石将军请求委任的请愿书草稿，以及信函草稿一份。

43. 至 44. 戴丰就任“第七路指挥官”时的讲话笔记。

45. 纸张一张，载有戴丰身世背景的粗略笔记。

46. 至 48. 戴丰致同胞关于其为国工作事项的宣言草稿。

49. 戴丰致李志明（Lee Ts Ming）的信函草稿，报告其下属的“叛变”情况。

50. 徐志道（Zee Ts Dau）求职信一封，日期为9月26日。

51. 油印通告一份，以戴丰和倪听雷（Nyi Ting Lai）的名义发出，劝告徐洪发不要向敌人投降。

1st Accused.

TAU FOONG (陶章) alias TAU CHING MAN (陶欽文)
Footung                                     /// W.J. Pryde
C.F.H. ..., 7.1.           25.4.40                          Hau A. F.

My name is Tau Foong, alias Tau Ching Man, age 39,
I was born at Oh Ang Tsung (陸行鎮), Footung, where my
father was the owner of a rice shop. My father died 10
years ago.

From the age of 7 years to 14 years I studied at
the Doo Tseu (杜家) School, Footung. On leaving school
I worked in my father's rice shop and when my father died
I became proprietor of this rice shop. When the Sino-Japanese
hostilities commenced in August 1937 I was a Captain in the
Peace Preservation Corps at Footung. When the Japanese
Forces occupied Footung in October 1937 I evacuated to
Shanghai. I was never in action against the Japanese
Forces at that time.

On arrival in Shanghai, I stayed at the Footung
Guild, of which I am a Committee Member, and obtained a
position on the staff of the Refugee Association attached to
this guild.

About December 1937 I returned to my native place
at the request of the shop keepers there, to organise a
Peace Preservation Corps, as the Chinese Forces had retreated
and there was no one to keep order in the district. I
enrolled 500 men and armed them with rifles etc., left behind
by the Peace Preservation Corps and Police Bureau. My object
at that time was to keep order in the district and not to
oppose the Japanese forces. My headquarters were located
at Yu Teh Li (余德里), The Yu Road. About the middle
of January 1938 Interpreter Samuel Wang To Lung (汪老楊).

第一被告。

TAU FOONG（陶章）别名 TAU CHING MAN（陶欽文）
浦东                                     /// W.J. Pryde
C.F.H ____ , 1月7日.           1940年4月25日                          Hau A. F.

我叫Tau Foong，别名Tau Ching Man，39岁，
出生于浦东Oh Ang Tsung（陸行鎮），我父亲在那里拥有一家米店。我父亲于10年前去世。

从7岁到14岁，我在浦东的Doo Tseu（杜家）学校读书。毕业后，我在父亲的米店工作，父亲去世后，我成为这家米店的店主。1937年8月中日敌对行动开始时，我是浦东保卫团的队长。1937年10月日军占领浦东时，我撤离至上海。当时我从未与日军发生过战斗。

抵达上海后，我住在浦东同乡会，我是该会的委员，并在隶属于该同乡会的难民协会中获得了一个职员职位。

约在1937年12月，应当地店主的请求，我返回家乡组织保卫团，因为中国军队已撤退，该地区无人维持秩序。我招募了500人，并用保卫团和警察局遗留的步枪等武器武装他们。我当时的目的是维持地区秩序，而非对抗日军。我的总部设在余德路（The Yu Road）的余德里（Yu Teh Li）。1938年1月中旬左右，翻译Samuel Wang To Lung（汪老楊）。

who was a commander of a Peace Preservation Corps in Pootung,
with headquarters in Tsu Tsah (川沙) City, and functioning
under the authority of the Nationalist Government, called
me to his headquarters and threatened to disarm my men unless
we enrolled under his command. I agreed to enroll and together
with my 500 men became part of his forces.

During March 1938 Tsung Ta Yang was defeated by the
Japanese Forces and his troops disbanded. My section of
500 men did not take part in this action and was left intact,
and the remnants from Tsung Ta Yang's forces joined up with
me and I then had approximately 3000 men under my command.
During May 1938 the forces in Pootung were reorganized and
became the Tsung Kyi National Salvation Army (忠义救国军).
I was appointed Captain of the 4th Company of the 1st Regiment
which was commanded by Li Ta Ming (李大明). General Dan Lih
(戴笠) was in command of the army in Pootung.

During July 1938 I came to Shanghai to seek medical
treatment. On recovering from my sickness I found that there
was trouble amongst the troops in Pootung so I did not return
there.

In December 1938 I obtained a position with the
Shanghai Refugee Boys and Girls Educational Institution
and am still employed there.

During June 1939 one named Hsiao (萧) came to see
me and stated that he had been sent by General Deng Feng Ying
(邓凤英), whose headquarters were at Suyang (宿阳) Jiangshou,
and who was reorganizing the guerrilla troops in Kiangsu.

他是浦东保卫团的指挥官，总部设在川沙（Tsu Tsah）城，在国民政府授权下行事，他召我到他的总部，威胁说除非我们编入他的麾下，否则就解除我部下的武装。我同意编入，我和我的500名部下一起成为他部队的一部分。

1938年3月期间，Tsung Ta Yang被日军击败，其部队解散。我那500人的分队未参与此次行动，建制保持完整，Tsung Ta Yang部队的残部加入了我，当时我手下约有3000人。1938年5月期间，浦东的部队进行了重组，成为忠义救国军。我被任命为第一团第四连连长，该团由李大明（Li Ta Ming）指挥。戴笠（Dan Lih）将军指挥浦东的军队。

1938年7月期间，我来上海求医。病愈后，我发现浦东部队内部出现麻烦，因此我没有回去。

1938年12月，我在上海难童教养院获得一个职位，至今仍受雇于此。

1939年6月期间，一个叫萧（Hsiao）的人来见我，称他是邓凤英（Deng Feng Ying）将军派来的，邓将军的总部在江苏宿阳（Suyang Jiangshou），正在重组江苏的游击队。

pages.en:
Siau further stated that General Dong Peng Ying had received
very good reports of my previous work in Pootung and requested
that I should accept the appointment as Major General i/c
of 7th Route Army of the South Kiangsu Guerrilla Troops
of the 3rd War Zone, National Military Committee. I agreed
to accept this position and received an official document
appointing me to this position. I have destroyed this document
I have received no pay for this appointment, I have no men
under my command and have not been active in any manner.
    In March 1940 I received a letter from General
Dong Peng Ying to the effect that he was coming to Shanghai
to interview me, but up to the present he has not arrived.
    I have not been outside of Shanghai since July 1938.

〔此处为手写签名〕
pages.zh:
萧（Siau）还称，董鹏英（Dong Peng Ying）将军对我之前在浦东的工作评价很好，并要求我接受第三战区国民军事委员会苏南游击队第七路军少将司令的任命。我同意接受这一职位，并收到了任命我为该职位的正式文件。我已销毁该文件。我未因该任命领取任何薪饷，手下无兵，也未以任何方式开展活动。
    1940年3月，我收到董鹏英将军的一封信，大意是他将来上海与我面谈，但截至目前他尚未到达。
    自1938年7月以来，我未曾离开过上海。

〔此处为手写签名〕

ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE GENDARMERIE.

At 1.50 p.m. 24.4.40, 2nd Sub-Lieut. Katoda
accompanied by four members of the Japanese Gendarmerie
came to C.B.H.Q.C.I. and requested assistance to visit
Lane 258, House 99 Wuting Road to arrest a male Chinese
named Dau Foong(陶峯 ) who, according to 2nd Sub-Lieut.
Katoda, is a Guerrilla Leader in the 3rd War Zone.

The U.S. Marine Corps and Gordon Road Station
were informed of the impending raid and assistance was
rendered by D.S.I.Pryde, D.S.s Massington, Sugimoto and
Sameshima and D.D.S.129 and the stated address, which
proved to be the premises of the Shanghai Refugee Boys
and Girls Institute(上海難童教養院) visited, and the wanted
man arrested in the General Office on the 1st floor of
this house.

The following are the particulars of this man:-
1st accused Dau Foong(陶峯 ) alias Dau Ching
Wan, age 30, Foctung M/Chief of General Affairs Depart-
ment, Shanghai Refugee Boys and Girls Institute, living
at house 86 D. St. St. St., Shanghai Refugee Zone, French
Concession. A search of the office desk used by this
man was made and a number of documents seized. A
superficial perusal of these documents has been made and

协助日本宪兵队。

1940年4月24日下午1时50分，片田（Katoda）二等副尉 accompanied by four members of the Japanese Gendarmerie（四名日本宪兵队员陪同）来到中央捕房总部刑事调查科，请求协助前往吴庭路（Wuting Road）258弄99号，逮捕一名叫陶峯（Dau Foong）的中国男子，据片田二等副尉称，此人是第三战区的游击队领导人。

美国海军陆战队和戈登路巡捕房获悉即将进行的突袭，并由副督察Pryde、警司Massington、Sugimoto和Sameshima以及副警司129号提供了协助，前往上述地址，该地址经查实为上海难童教养院的 premises（场所），并在该楼房一楼的总办公室逮捕了这名通缉犯。

Police was obtained at 4.30 p.m. and D.S.I.Pryde,
D.S.Sugimoto and D.S.I.Yang Shi Kwang searched the 1st
accused home at 26 D. Si Ou Ka Za, Zikawei but only
three photographs of the accused himself were seized.

As the accused admits being concerned in
guerrilla activities a full statement will be taken
from him on 25.4.40.

The 2nd accused Shah Liang states he called at
258/99 Wuting Road to see the 1st accused who is an old
friend of his. That he had not seen the 1st accused
for over one year and having seen in a newspaper that the
1st accused was now working at the Refugee Institute he
decided to call on him.

D.S.Hessington and Sameshima, D.S.I.Zia Wei
Fung and two members of the Japanese Gendarmerie
searched the 2nd accused home at 10 Bang Dai Li, Jess-
field Road at 6 p.m. but nothing incriminating was
found. 2nd Sub-Lieut. Takeda requested that this man be
detained for further enquiries.

Both accused have been detained in Central Cells.
Neither of the accused were residents of the
settlement prior to the hostilities.

〔此处转录不清〕
C. B. Pryor.

于下午4时30分获得警方许可，副督察Pryde、警司Sugimoto和副督察杨世光（Yang Shi Kwang）搜查了第一被告位于徐家汇D. Si Ou Ka Za路26号的住所，但仅查获了三张被告本人的照片。

由于被告承认参与游击活动，将于1940年4月25日对其录取完整供词。

第二被告夏良（Shah Liang）称，他去吴庭路258弄99号拜访第一被告，第一被告是他的老朋友。他说已有一年多未见第一被告，在报纸上看到第一被告现在在难童教养院工作后，决定去拜访他。

警司Hessington和Sameshima、副督察谢维芳（Xia Wei Fung）以及两名日本宪兵队员于下午6时搜查了第二被告位于杰斯菲尔德路（Jessfield Road）邦代里10号的住所，但未发现任何罪证。竹田（Takeda）二等副尉要求拘留此人以作进一步查询。

两名被告均被拘押在中央拘留所。
在敌对行动开始前，两名被告均非公共租界居民。

〔此处转录不清〕
C. B. Pryor.

2nd accused Shah Liang( 夏 良 ) 35, Poetung,

called there to see the 1st accused Dau Foong
alias Dan Ching Yun and at the request of the Japanese
Gendarmerie this man was detained and together with the
1st accused brought to C.B.H.Q. for enquiries.

The st accused Dau Foong alias Dan Ching Yun
on being questioned admits being concerned in guerrilla
activities. He also stated that he is a director of
the Poetung Guild, 1484 Avenue Edward VII, and his
mail is delivered to this address.

D.S.P. Harrington and Interpreter, D.S.I. Sia
Sui Fong accompanied by 3 members of the Japanese
Gendarmerie visited the Poetung Guild at 6:30 p.m.
when it was verified that the accused was a member of
the Executive of this Guild and had attended a meeting
there on 13-4-42 but that no mail had been received therein

第二被告 夏良（Shah Liang），35岁，浦东人，职业屠夫，居住在杰斯菲尔德路（Jessfield Road）统德里（Tung Tai Li）10号，

第一被告陶峯（Dau Foong），别名丹青云（Dan Ching Yun）在接受讯问时，承认参与游击活动。他还称自己是爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）1484号浦东同乡会的董事，他的邮件寄送至该地址。

警司Harrington和翻译、副督察谢瑞芳（Sia Sui Fung）在三名日本宪兵队员的陪同下，于下午6:30访问了浦东同乡会，经核实，被告是该同乡会执行委员会成员，并曾于1942年4月13日参加在那里举行的一次会议，但该处已有一段时间未收到任何邮件。
